extracted.intended_audience: legislators, statesmen, political thinkers, and the politically engaged public
extracted.subtask_description: Critical standards and guiding principles for designing, evaluating, and implementing constitutions and large-scale political reforms, with emphasis on prudence, social means, and the effects on society. The guidance addresses representation, local government, pace of reform, and the moral/Practical considerations legislators should observe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confront difficulty rather than evade it
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose everywhere seems to have been to evade and slip aside from difficulty. This it has been the glory of the great masters in all the arts to confront, and to overcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wrestling with difficulty strengthens understanding and prevents superficial solutions; policymakers should not seek easy or fallacious facilities but should take on hard problems so their solutions become durable and extend human understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve useful parts while reforming
rubrics_metrics.description: At once to preserve and to reform is quite another thing. When the useful parts of an old establishment are kept, and what is superadded is to be fitted to what is retained...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reformers should identify and retain valuable elements of existing institutions and fit new measures to them, exercising steady attention, comparison, and ingenuity so as to avoid throwing away useful arrangements in the name of novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proceed slowly; use time as an assistant
rubrics_metrics.description: It is one of the excellences of a method in which time is amongst the assistants, that its operation is slow, and in some cases almost imperceptible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Circumspection and caution are duties when altering the condition of sentient beings; incremental steps allow observation of effects and correction from 'light to light' — patience will achieve more than force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legislator temperament: sensibility, love of kind, and self-fear
rubrics_metrics.description: The true lawgiver ought to have a heart full of sensibility. He ought to love and respect his kind, and to fear himself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective lawmakers should be humane, modest, and cautious; they may perceive ultimate aims intuitively but must move deliberately to avoid harming people by rash changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political change must be wrought by social means
rubrics_metrics.description: Political arrangement, as it is a work for social ends, is to be only wrought by social means. There mind must conspire with mind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Law and reform require the cooperation and consensus of minds across society; reforms imposed without social engagement are unlikely to produce lasting good.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value practical experience over abstract paradox
rubrics_metrics.description: If circumspection and caution are a part of wisdom... I have never yet seen any plan which has not been mended by the observations of those who were much inferior in understanding to the person who took the lead in the business.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeal to experience: practical observation and the input of many minds (including those considered inferior) improve designs; abstract paradoxes or rhetorical paradoxes are poor foundations for policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Have a presiding principle and cohesive design
rubrics_metrics.description: To proceed in this manner, that is, to proceed with a presiding principle and a prolific energy, is with me the criterion of profound wisdom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constitutional design should be organized around a clear, stable principle (a 'presiding principle') that provides continuity and guides subsequent adjustments, promoting coherence rather than ad hoc fixes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid haste, charlatans, and radical adventurers
rubrics_metrics.description: By their violent haste, and their defiance of the process of Nature, they are delivered over blindly to every projector and adventurer, to every alchemist and empiric.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rapid, radical overhauls open the door to opportunists and untested schemes; good reform requires skepticism toward simplistic cures and confidence in regular, proven methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judge constitutions by practical effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Old establishments are tried by their effects. If the people are happy, united, wealthy, and powerful, we presume the rest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rather than purely theoretical consistency, evaluate political systems by observable outcomes — unity, prosperity, public happiness — and allow experience to guide theory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware purely theoretical systems disconnected from habit and usage
rubrics_metrics.description: In a new and merely theoretic system, it is expected that every contrivance shall appear, on the face of it, to answer its ends... The means taught by experience may be better suited to political ends than those contrived in the original project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theorists who redesign institutions without regard to historical practice and local habits risk producing brittle, impractical systems; reforms should account for accommodations evolved by use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not rely on mechanical/geometrical bases for representation
rubrics_metrics.description: They propose to rest the whole local and general legislature on three bases ... the basis of territory; the basis of population; and the basis of contribution. At first view this geometrical basis of theirs presents not much to admire or to blame.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mechanical divisions (e.g., rigid square geographical partitions) or simple numerical schemes do not substitute for political judgment; representation schemes must reflect real social relations, not abstract measurement alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualifications for suffrage must not subvert natural equality
rubrics_metrics.description: First, the voters in the Canton... are to have a qualification... You order him to buy the right which you before told him Nature had given to him gratuitously at his birth...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Property or tax-paying qualifications that exclude the poorest contradict claims of natural equality and create a new aristocracy by practice; voting qualifications should not undermine fundamental rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation by contribution must relate to persons, not just districts
rubrics_metrics.description: The additional share in the third portion of representation ... is made to regard the district only, and not the individuals in it who pay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If wealth or contribution is a basis for influence, it should affect individuals or explicit classes of rich persons, not simply produce unequal districtweights that fail to protect the actual contributors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer indirect (consumption) contribution as a measure of wealth over direct contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: The indirect contribution, that which arises from duties on consumption, is in truth a better standard, and follows and discovers wealth more naturally than this of direct contribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indirect taxes on consumption distribute the burden and reveal real economic participation more fairly than narrow direct-contribution measures that misattribute wealth to localities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid systems where constitution depends on the tax system
rubrics_metrics.description: As they have contrived matters, their taxation does not so much depend on their constitution as their constitution on their taxation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constitutions should be stable and not made variable by changes in taxation; tying representation or rights to fluctuating tax assessments produces constitutional uncertainty and internal controversies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure consistency between multiple bases of representation
rubrics_metrics.description: To compare together the three bases... we cannot avoid observing that the principle which the committee call the basis of population does not begin to operate from the same point with the two other principles ... The consequence is ... the most absurd inequality produced by the operation of the former on the two latter principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When multiple principles (territory, population, contribution) are combined, designers must resolve their differing starting points and avoid producing contradictory or absurd inequalities between groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include moral and political considerations — account for human passions and interests
rubrics_metrics.description: It is remarkable, that, in a great arrangement of mankind, not one reference whatsoever is to be found to anything moral or anything politic, -- nothing that relates to the concerns, the actions, the passions, the interests of men.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constitutional design must explicitly consider human motivations, customs, passions, and interests rather than ignoring these in favor of abstract metaphysics, geometry, or arithmetic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve national coherence: avoid severing the country into independent republics
rubrics_metrics.description: You cannot but perceive in this scheme, that it has a direct and immediate tendency to sever France into a variety of republics, and to render them totally independent of each other...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decentralization and local independence must be balanced with constitutional mechanisms of coherence, connection, and subordination; otherwise the nation risks fragmentation and loss of unity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain local knowledge and civil habituation in local offices
rubrics_metrics.description: Magistrates and collectors of revenue are now no longer acquainted with their districts, bishops with their dioceses, or curates with their parishes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local governance should preserve officers' familiarity with their districts and the civil habits that sustain republican discipline; creating officials who are strangers to their localities undermines effective administration and civic cohesion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be wary of democratic multiplication of offices that create corrupting incentives
rubrics_metrics.description: The increase of representation within his province sets up nine persons more, and as many more than nine as there may be democratic candidates, to cabal and intrigue and to flatter the people at his expense and to his oppression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creating many democratic offices to 'reward' or balance interests generates salaries, ambition, and opportunism that can exploit the wealthy and distort governance; institutional incentives matter.
